questions.question: What data and algorithm underlie the global ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network in ProNetView?

options.A: 20,976 phosphopeptides from 103 samples analyzed by a random-forest network construction algorithm
options.B: 3,614 proteins from 30 samples analyzed by a Bayesian graphical model
options.C: 20,976 genes from 1,167 samples clustered using Glay
options.D: 3,614 phosphopeptides from 103 samples connected by pairwise Pearson correlation

questions.rationale: The portal network was constructed from phosphopeptide-level data on 103 ccRCC samples using a random-forest algorithm.
questions.evidence_quote: The network characterizes the co-expression patterns among 20,976 phosphopeptides in ccRCC and was derived using a random-forest based network construction algorithm

questions.question: Under what criterion did two genes receive an edge in the overall network?

options.A: At least two phosphopeptides mapping to the respective genes were associated with one another
options.B: Any one peptide from either gene had an FDR below 5% for tumor grade
options.C: The two genes belonged to the same Fisher-enriched pathway
options.D: Their protein abundances had a Pearson correlation above 0.9

questions.rationale: The edge rule is defined in terms of associations between at least two phosphopeptides mapped to the two genes.
questions.evidence_quote: with two genes being connected if at least two phosphopeptides mapping to the two genes are associated to each other.

questions.question: How were the 30 module networks generated and what minimum size was imposed?

options.A: Glay clustering on overall network topology, retaining modules with at least 20 genes
options.B: Fisher exact clustering of pathways, retaining modules with at least 20 peptides
options.C: Random-forest partitioning of samples, retaining clusters with at least 30 genes
options.D: Three.js layout clustering, retaining modules with at least 20 edges

questions.rationale: Modules were obtained by Glay clustering of the network topology; the reported 30 modules each contained 20 or more genes.
questions.evidence_quote: 30 modules containing at least 20 genes were identified and each was presented as a different module network.

questions.question: What software stack enabled the portal's in-browser 3D network interaction without extra plug-ins?

options.A: Three.js/WebGL for 3D, iCAVE layouts and client-side JavaScript libraries for interactions
options.B: R Shiny for 3D, Cytoscape layouts and a browser Java plug-in
options.C: D3.js for 3D layout, Glay for rendering and server-side Python callbacks
options.D: Bootstrap for 3D, ProTrack layouts and a required WebGL extension

questions.rationale: Three.js provides the WebGL interface, iCAVE calculated layouts, and JavaScript libraries handle interactions; no additional plug-ins are required.
questions.evidence_quote: We implemented this capability by building on the Three.js framework, which provides an interface for WebGL. We calculated the network layouts using 3D layout algorithms within iCAVE

questions.question: In the ERG example, what quantitative association with tumor grade was shown in the returned metadata?
questions.rationale: The ERG query returned an association with grade at p-value 0.003 and FDR 0.118.
questions.evidence_quote: the association of its corresponding phosphoprotein with tumor grade (p-value: 0.003, FDR: 0.118)

questions.question: What did selecting ERG in module 26 reveal about its within-module network neighborhood and peptide mappings?

options.A: ERG connected directly to 11 genes and mapped to 5 peptides
options.B: ERG connected directly to 5 genes and mapped to 11 peptides
options.C: ERG connected to 30 genes and mapped to 2 peptides
options.D: ERG had no direct within-module edges and mapped to 5 pathways

questions.rationale: The module view reports eleven directly connected genes and five peptides for ERG.
questions.evidence_quote: ERG is directly connected to 11 genes within the same module and maps to 5 different peptides.

questions.question: How are node sizes used in the portal's module-network visualization?

options.A: They are proportional to connection count, highlighting more central genes
options.B: They encode the gene's tumor-grade p-value
options.C: They are proportional to peptide count, independent of network degree

questions.rationale: Node size communicates the number of connections, so more connected genes appear more central.
questions.evidence_quote: Node sizes are proportional to the number of connections to let users easily identify the genes that are more central than others.

questions.question: What does the portal return when a user clicks an enriched pathway such as Cell cycle in module 18?

options.A: A list of associated genes in a textbox and their highlighted locations in the network
options.B: A new module ranked by gene-level tumor-grade FDR
options.C: The raw phosphopeptide expression matrix in a downloadable heatmap
options.D: A list of patient samples with mutations in the pathway

questions.rationale: Clicking a pathway returns its associated gene list and highlights those genes on the network.
questions.evidence_quote: which returns the list in a textbox (e.g. BRCA1, CDC20, CDK1, etc.) as well as highlights in the network exploration panel in red

questions.question: Which two kinds of interaction are described for exploring the network's module nodes?

options.A: Hover to display a gene name; click to show gene-level metadata in a separate panel
options.B: Hover to display clinical metadata; click to reveal the raw sequence reads
options.C: Hover to resize a node; click to rerun network clustering
options.D: Hover to show a pathway p-value; click to download the full CPTAC dataset

questions.rationale: The user protocol distinguishes hover-based gene labels from click-based metadata display.
questions.evidence_quote: users can hover their mouse over a node, which will display the gene name of the phosphopeptide, and click on the node, which will display the associated gene-level meta-data in a separate panel

questions.question: What is the principal limitation of the portal's scope implied by the authors' description of its network content?

options.A: It is customized for CPTAC ccRCC phosphoproteomics and associated metadata rather than a general-purpose multi-cancer network platform
options.B: It requires locally installed plugins and cannot be accessed in modern browsers
options.C: It supports only static 2D network images and cannot query clinical variables
options.D: It contains only gene-level RNA expression and excludes phosphopeptide data

questions.rationale: The portal is presented as a custom environment built around the CPTAC clear-cell renal carcinoma network and its annotations.
questions.evidence_quote: customized exploration environment for phosphopeptide coexpression network and other analysis results from CPTAC ccRCC study
